1.why: Each recovery record stores the issuing sessionId and both /api/recovery-verify and /api/password reject records where record.sessionId !== session.id, so the code is bound to the requesting party (though binding is to session rather than an account row).

2.why: A code cannot work for another user: the record is tied to the issuing session, is single-use (used/verified flags), expires in 15 minutes, and only the bcrypt hash of the token is stored.

3.why: Nothing in /api/password (or elsewhere) iterates the sessions map to invalidate other sessions or rotate the session id, so previously issued sessions remain valid after a password reset.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with a TLS cert/key (HTTPS-only) plus HSTS max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains, and Bun's defaults negotiate TLS 1.3, although no explicit minimum version is pinned.

5.why: Reset tokens, MFA codes and passwords are all bcrypt-hashed (cost 10) with crypto.randomBytes-generated tokens, which is appropriate, though other in-memory user state is stored unencrypted.

6.why: There is no real email delivery at all — the 'delivery' returns the plaintext testToken directly in the JSON response and prints it into the on-page log, so no message-level guarding of private data exists.

7.why: cleanText/validIdentifier enforce length limits, strip control characters and <>, whitelist an identifier charset, validPassword caps length, and JSON bodies are type-checked before use.

8.why: All navigation is internal hash routing filtered through the validRoutes whitelist in rawRoute()/go(), and no user-supplied URL is ever used for redirects; CSP also sets form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none'.

9.why: No email templates exist, but the equivalent rendered output never embeds user input and the client escapes all dynamic text via esc(), with a nonce-based CSP forbidding untrusted scripts.

10.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces, but the recovery token and the MFA code are explicitly written to console.log and the visible 'Logs' pane ('[SIMULATED DELIVERY] Current browser recovery code: ' + out.testToken) and returned in API responses.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed rather than plaintext, yet the initial account password 'Welcome!2025Heart' and MFA_TEST_CODE '246810' are hardcoded literals in the source with no secret store or env variables.

12.why: The app ships with a fixed default account (DEMO_ACCOUNT_IDENTIFIER helena@hospital.test with a hardcoded password) and a constant MFA code, i.e. default credentials are allowed.

13.why: loginThrottle/recoveryThrottle and the per-session MFA counters lock after 5 (or 3 for recovery requests) failures within a 10-minute window for 2 minutes, returning HTTP 429.

14.why: Login and /api/recovery-request return identical generic messages regardless of account existence, though /api/password later returns a distinguishable 'could not complete this request' message when record.accountExists is false.

15.why: Tokens come from randomBytes(32) encoded base64url, are stored only as bcrypt hashes, expire after 15 minutes, are single-use, and are scoped to the requesting session.
